rv.q: Gilman delivers with 'Swing State' an engrossing work of intense melancholy, filled with sympathy for its characters, and for the country.
Although SWING STATE sometimes drifts too much for my taste, the performances anchor the immense humanity in the characters.
This play is intense, heart-warming, and a tear-jerker, all rolled into an hour and forty-five minutes of great theater — it's Chicago theater at its best!
Rebecca Gilman's incredibly riveting new drama, currently enjoying its much lauded World Premiere at the Goodman Theatre, solidifies this writer as one of our finest American playwrights.

Goodman's highly personal Swing State is about people, not politics By Karen Topham October 20, 2022. October 20, 2022. Chicago Reviews Rebecca Gilman's new play Swing State , now playing at the Goodman Theatre, is not, as you might imagine from the title, about politics. At least not overtly.
"Swing State" is another riveting script from the Pulitzer-nominated playwright.
Powerful performances and top-notch writing make Swing State a highly relatable post-Covid play – one that you might just find sticks with you for days.
Gillman, Falls and the ensemble deliver human imperfection perfectly.
The acting and direction in the production are uniformly excellent.
Sharply directed by Robert Falls, who loves doing Ms. Gilman's works on a set designed by Todd Rosenthal, you will feel that you are truly in a rural home in rural Wisconsin.

cn.t: Gilman's character-driven drama earns strong praise for its intimate portrayal of grief and fractured community in rural Wisconsin, though it's more about personal struggles than politics despite its provocative title.
